what_it_does: Designing a processor involves choosing among thousands of interacting configuration options (cache sizes, pipeline depths, number of execution units, etc.). Bayesian optimization is a technique that intelligently picks which configurations to actually build and test, learning from each result to steer toward better designs with fewer trials. But when the configuration space is very large, the internal prediction model of standard Bayesian optimization makes large errors, and the method also struggles to obey hard constraints (for example, the chip must fit within a power budget). SRBO adds a self-review step inspired by teacher-student learning — a second model critiques and corrects the first model's predictions — and uses an ensemble of models (several models whose disagreement signals uncertainty) to handle constraints more reliably. The target application is RISC-V processor design, where the technique reduces the number of costly simulations needed to find a good design.
